summary: Players build a personal deck of cattle cards and repeatedly drive herds down the trail from Texas to Kansas City, visiting buildings along the way to upgrade cards, hire staff, and manage hazards before cashing in the herd for money and points. Over several trips the trail fills up with buildings (yours and others'), a shared railroad gets extended westward, and your deck/tableau snowballs into a tight personal engine.
praised: deeply interlocking systems (deck building, hand management, worker placement, railroad) that mesh without feeling bloated
high replayability from randomized building setup each game
satisfying sense of engine progression across multiple trail runs
meaningful, tense decisions on nearly every turn
criticised: steep rules overhead and long first play/teach
analysis paralysis from the sheer number of viable strategies
can feel mean when opponents build on prime trail spots you wanted and charge you fees
early turns can feel slow before engines come online

interaction.kind: shared board contested via building placement and fees, racing for limited spots
interaction.detail: The trail, Kansas City building plots, and the railroad track are a shared, contested space: players build on specific spots (locking others out or forcing them to pay a toll to use your building), race to be first to deliver along the delivery track for bonus points, and compete for limited jobs and railroad stations. Each player's own deck, hand, and personal tableau of workers/buildings remain private and non-interactive, so most turns are solitaire-engine optimization punctuated by contested placement moments.

subsystems: building network (constructing and renting out buildings)
sources: points from delivery track position each time you reach Kansas City
bonus points for being first to reach certain cities
points from buildings you've constructed (value increases with building tier)
points from railroad stations built and track placement
points from hazards removed via Cowboys
objective/certificate tiles collected during the game
leftover money converted to points at game end
scoring.how_you_win: The game ends once the building-construction track in San Francisco is filled (or after a fixed number of rounds in some variants), and whoever has accumulated the most total points from deliveries, buildings, railroad, hazards, objectives, and leftover cash wins.
